title: Michael Hunstad - Institutional Trends in Factor Investing (S3E9)

reader_summary.headline: Michael Hunstead, head of quantitative strategies at Northern Trust.
reader_summary.overview: Michael Hunstead, head of quantitative strategies at Northern Trust. Our conversation centers around the four key trends Michael is seeing among institutional allocators in the factor space today. one, the adoption of factors to manage concentration risk in market cap-weighted benchmarks, two, a move from single to multi-factor implementations, three.

key_points.text: one, the adoption of factors to manage concentration risk in market cap-weighted benchmarks, two, a move from single to multi-factor implementations, three.
key_points.evidence_quote: one, the adoption of factors to manage concentration risk in market cap-weighted benchmarks, two, a move from single to multi-factor implementations, three, using factors to de-risk equity exposure, and four, a tactical tilt towards value.

key_points.text: But Michael isn't afraid to get in the weeds.

key_points.text: He discusses the risks of unintended exposures at length and at one point even explains the importance of matching decay speeds of different factor signals within multi-factor implementations..

thesis: Dr. Michael Hunstead argues that institutional investors are increasingly adopting factor strategies to manage concentration risk in market-cap weighted benchmarks, de-risk equity portfolios via quality and low volatility factors, and tilt towards value due to attractive valuations. He contends that the recent struggles of value stocks are cyclical rather than structural, citing historical precedents and current trading multiples that are significantly below historical averages.
